builds.name: Reference: Contact fighter
builds.goal: Reference for Jarvan IV: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: An initiating fighter who combines flag-and-lance knock-ups with an arena that holds enemies for allied damage. Measure E/Q knockup and trapped-target contact; enemies can escape Cataclysm. Compare physical pick damage with a lower-income initiation/protection route. Stridebreaker access and conditional Sundered Sky sustain may buy time for repeated kit damage.
builds.summary: Stridebreaker access and conditional Sundered Sky sustain may buy time for repeated kit damage.
testPlan: Kit question for Jarvan IV: Measure E/Q knockup and trapped-target contact; enemies can escape Cataclysm. Compare physical pick damage with a lower-income initiation/protection route.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then Sundered Sky) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Stridebreaker access and conditional Sundered Sky sustain may buy time for repeated kit damage. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Jarvan IV extends his lance, dealing physical damage and lowering the Armor of enemies in its path. Additionally, this will pull Jarvan to his Demacian Standard, knocking up enemies in his path. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.

builds.name: Cadence Target Cycle
builds.summary: Compare fresh-target cadence attacks with repeated locked-target attacks.
builds.goal: Compare fresh-target cadence attacks with repeated locked-target attacks.
builds.hypothesis: P gives current-health physical damage with a per-target cooldown. Q armor reduction helps the next attack; E grants attack speed and Trinity/Sundered Sky reward an actual fresh-target attack. Stridebreaker aids moving among targets rather than repeatedly hitting a P-locked opponent.
testPlan: Required state: Two reachable targets with separate P cooldowns and Q applied first.
Compare fresh-target cadence attacks with repeated locked-target attacks; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Target switching loses focus damage or exposes Jarvan to both enemies.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Attack speed does not remove the per-target passive cooldown.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Trinity Force, Sundered Sky, Stridebreaker, Black Cleaver, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.
